quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how much alcohol their body absorbs. Biological sex, the amount of food in the stomach, and how many drinks consumed also matter. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, keep your seat belt on. Press your body and head firmly against your seat to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel tightly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to the right lane when you can see the passed car's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line mean on a highway?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the lane on your right.
Move to the lane on your left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane on your right.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, stay in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. Use the right lane if you are driving slower than traffic.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold, wet weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw later. On cold, wet days, watch for ice in shaded spots.

questions.question: If a car hits you from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If a car hits you from behind, your body will move backward. Press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: You have a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block cross traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking the intersection.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicles crossing or merging that are close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light with a green arrow. When can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: When you come to a complete stop first.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. Before turning, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers cannot see you if you are directly behind them. Keep more distance from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not brake. Steer to correct the skid until your vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead when it is dark. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare will blind you.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You are not allowed to pass.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass. Only pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop if needed. You may continue if there is no conflicting traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire suddenly goes flat while driving?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car going straight. Slow down by taking your foot off the gas and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. You cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork or maintenance is present.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of construction, maintenance, or roadwork. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe in work areas. Traffic fines are often doubled in these zones.

questions.question: What should you do as you approach the top of a hill?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. Another vehicle might be stopped there. Adjust your speed so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle or property.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline allow you to do?

options.text: You must stay within your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic moves in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over their left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over their left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. How should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When trapped between oncoming traffic and parked cars, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: A vehicle cuts in front of you suddenly. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and step on the brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: What is the main idea of defensive driving?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
They expect no breaks and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers anticipate mistakes other drivers might make and prepare to react to them.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
At the posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another car at night. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. Impatient drivers behind you may take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead of your vehicle:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or sharp turns.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or sharp turns.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead. This lets you stop or change lanes smoothly, making you a safer driver and helping traffic flow steadily.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Then vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If another vehicle is following you too closely on a two-lane road:

options.text: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage them to pass you. Change lanes if possible.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to move the car back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Let your speed slow down, check for traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly. This can cause you to lose control or enter another lane.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: On a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, stay off the brakes, and turn your steering wheel in the direction the car is skidding. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.
Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up in the travel lane or on the shoulder. Continue to the next exit or crossroad instead. Drivers do not expect a vehicle backing up on the roadway, and this will likely cause a crash.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road, entrance, or exit. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control devices in a work zone.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School zone or crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Do not stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.
Often leads to high-risk decision-making.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decisions while driving.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can be on any track, at any time, coming from either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.
